blocks.title: Common errors
blocks.md: Never infer a limit from an isolated function value. Distinguish a derivative from an accumulation function. Keep exact fractions and radicals, and keep the input separate from the value it attains.

blocks.title: Written exam practice
blocks.md: Use exact notation on paper. Check answers by reversing the operation when possible: differentiate an antiderivative, test a sign chart, or plug the optimizer back into the constraint.

blocks.title: Continuity followed by a derivative
blocks.problem: Let $f(x)=(x^2-4)/(x-2)$ for $x\ne2$. Extend it continuously to 2 and find the derivative there.

steps.title: Extend continuously
steps.why: A continuous extension uses the nearby limit.

steps.title: Differentiate the extension
steps.md: After assigning $f(2)=4$, the extended function is $x+2$ for every x.
steps.why: Its difference quotient is 1, including at 2.

blocks.title: FTC instead of an antiderivative
blocks.problem: Find where $A(x)=\int_0^{x}(3-t^2)\,dt$ has an absolute maximum on $[0,3]$.

steps.title: Find the derivative
steps.why: The variable upper bound has derivative 1.

steps.title: Check signs
steps.why: Increase followed by decrease on the whole interval gives the absolute maximum.

blocks.title: Distance from signed velocity
blocks.problem: A particle has velocity $v(t)=3t^2-12$ m/s. Find total distance over $[0,3]$.

steps.title: Find the split
steps.md: The velocity turns from negative to positive at $t=2$.
steps.why: Distance sums each leg without cancellation.
